title: Labeling quickfire decision matrix
content:
Purpose:
Quick decision aid for labelers and reviewers when a single example could map to multiple labels or fall into boundary/overlap cases. Goal: reduce adjudication time for microdisagreements while preserving recall for high-impact signals.

How to use: read the row that most closely matches the example, follow the guidance, add a short rationale in the comment field of the annotation UI (1-2 sentences). If uncertain, mark ABSTAIN and add the quick reason tag.

DECISION MATRIX (compact, human readable):
- Short span (<= 5 tokens) | clear lexical boundary | canonical type candidate present -> Apply label, confidence HIGH; no split.
- Short span | punctuation-only boundary ambiguity (e.g., dash/paren) -> normalize punctuation then label; prefer include if semantic chunk intact.
- Long span (> 5 tokens) | contains internal conjunctions or appositive clauses -> attempt to split into minimal entity spans; label both if independent. If only one is target, mark primary label and add SUBSPAN tag.
- Overlapping spans | one spans the other and both plausible -> label the smaller span (specific) as primary, larger as CONTEXTUAL with low priority. Add "overlap:kept-small" rationale.
- Overlap with nested types (e.g., Organization inside Address) -> label both when downstream consumers care; otherwise choose type used by most recent evals (see linked_artifacts).
- Code / inline JSON / SQL snippets -> treat as LITERAL_TEXT; DO NOT extract named entities inside code unless domain rule exists.
- URLs, emails, tokens with brackets/anchor text -> extract visible text only; for tracking params or IDs, mark ID token as separate label (ID_DEVICE, ID_SESSION) when present.
- Emojis and reactions at sentence end -> ignore for entity spans; but capture as sentiment_marker if label set includes sentiment.
- Ambiguous numeric sequences ("202101" vs "2021-01") -> prefer ISO-like normalization; if parsing uncertain, mark NUM_UNNORMALIZED and add example to review queue.

EXEMPLARS (kept short):
- "Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) reported..." -> label: Organization=Apple, Ticker=AAPL (keep both). Rationale: ticker is a distinct token used downstream.
- "john.doe@example.com" -> label: EMAIL=john.doe@example.com (treat as single token).
- "Room 12A-3" -> label: ROOM=Room 12A-3 (include alphanumerics and dash).
- "Ref: 8/12" -> context needed; if in invoice context, label=DATE_PART; otherwise ABSTAIN.

QUALITY/CONFIDENCE GUIDELINES:
- HIGH: unambiguous lexical match to examples in spec, token boundaries clean.
- MEDIUM: minor punctuation or casing issues but core token present. Add normalization note.
- LOW: semantic ambiguity or partial overlap; prefer ABSTAIN.

TRIAGE & REVIEW FLOW (practical):
- Labeler marks ABSTAIN -> automated triage to Senior Adjudicator queue (LAB-3412).
- If the same ABSTAIN reason occurs 10+ times in a week, create a ticket and attach 10 examples.
- For systematic parser failures (tokenization causing split entities), leave a one-line repro and tag as tokenization-bug. Reference: dataset-tools PR 128.

FAST RULES (one-liners) FOR QUICKFIRE DECISIONS:
- If it's an ID-like contiguous alnum string with separators -> capture whole as ID.
- If entity spans two syntactic units connected by "and" -> split unless templates indicate single combined entity.
- If punctuation sits inside a named entity (apostrophes, periods in initials) -> include them (e.g., O'Neil, J.K.).
- If a label would change product behavior (billing, legal, privacy) -> escalate immediately.

COMMON EDGECASE PATTERNS WE SEE (notes to self):
- Mixed-language names: first token in Latin, rest in non-Latin script -> tokenizers sometimes split; add to tokenization-bug list.
- Dates without year in logs -> assume most recent past date unless context indicates schedule. Mark as inferred-date in comment.
- Hyphenated compound adjectives vs compound proper nouns ("New-York-style" vs "New-York") -> prefer noun-inclusion if capitalized.

SAMPLE ANNOTATIONS (what to write in rationale field):
- "Kept ticker as separate label because downstream billing maps tickers to market IDs."
- "Abstained: ambiguous date format; flagged for collection team."
- "Split: two person names joined by conjunction; both are distinct entities for contact extraction."

OPEN QUESTIONS / TO-FIX LIST (personal TODOs):
- Define standard for including honorifics (Dr., Ms.) — currently inconsistent; propose rule by end of quarter.
- Create 20 canonical counterexamples for overlapping org/location cases.
- Add a short regex library for common ID tokens (order IDs, session IDs) to shared repo.

SLACK / REF NOTES:
- See #labeling-bugs for recent tokenization spikes (message thread on 2024-12-02 by @jonah).
- Quick demo video saved in Confluence (Labeling-Std-V2) for new hires — reference for training.

FINAL NOTE (tone):
This is meant to speed decisions, not replace adjudication. Keep comments short and factual. If you feel the matrix doesn't cover a pattern, capture 3 examples and drop into LAB-3412 for discussion.

— MK
